Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
Yes — that's very helpful, and it explains the slow speeds. All three of those findings are things you'll want to change. Here's what to do, in order:

**1. Turn ON Mobile Data**
- Go to **Settings → Cellular (or Mobile Network)**
- Toggle **Mobile Data** to **ON**

This is the main switch that lets your phone use the carrier network for internet.

**2. Turn ON Data Roaming**
- In the same **Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options** menu
- Toggle **Data Roaming** to **ON**

Good news here: I already confirmed on your account that **roaming is provisioned and enabled on your line (555-123-2002) at no extra cost**. The line side is fully set up — your phone just had the local switch flipped off, which was blocking you.

**3. Change your network mode off 2G**

This is the other half of the slow-speed problem. A 2G connection is very old technology — it's far too slow for anything beyond basic calls/texts, and it can't reliably support data or picture messaging.

- Go to **Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options → Voice & Data** (may also be called **Network Mode** or **Preferred Network Type**)
- Select **4G/5G Auto** or **5G On** (whichever appears — you want the option that prefers 4G and 5G)

**4. Restart your phone**

After making these changes, power your phone off and back on so the new settings take full effect and it reconnects to the best available network in France.

**One thing to set expectations:** even with everything configured correctly, roaming speeds can be slower than what you're used to at home, since you're connecting through a local French partner network. And your signal is currently showing as poor — if it stays poor after the restart, try moving somewhere with a clearer view or closer to a window, as indoor spaces can weaken signal significantly.

To summarize the full picture on your account:
- **Line status:** Active, not suspended
- **Roaming:** Enabled on your line at no cost
- **Data:** 2 GB refueled, ~1.9 GB remaining through **Feb 28**
- **Nothing else needs changing on the account side** — it's all on the device settings now

Could you make those three setting changes and restart? Let me know what your signal and network type show afterward, and we can go from there if it's still not right.

turns.thought:
Excellent progress — that's exactly the result we wanted. Going from 2G/poor to 5G/Excellent resolves the main cause of your slow speeds, and combined with the 2 GB refuel you should now have a solid connection.

On your two questions:

**Data Saver — yes, I'd recommend turning this OFF.**

Data Saver is designed to reduce your data consumption by restricting background data usage, and it can genuinely make apps and services feel slow or unresponsive — web pages may load partially, apps may not refresh in the background, and media may be compressed. Since you're roaming and want reliable performance, it's working against you right now.

- Go to **Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options → Data Saver** (or **Settings → Connections → Data Usage → Data Saver**)
- Toggle it **OFF**

Note: switching to 5G means you may use data faster than on 2G, so it's worth keeping an eye on your remaining allowance (roughly **1.9 GB**, resetting **Feb 28**).

**VPN — this one depends, so let me ask rather than assume.**

A VPN encrypts your traffic and routes it through a remote server, and that extra hop can reduce your speed noticeably — sometimes significantly if the server is distant or busy. But I can't see how well *your* VPN is currently performing from here; that's a reading only your phone can give me.

Two things would help me advise you properly:

1. **Do you actually need the VPN** right now — for example for work access, or to reach home-country content or banking sites while you're in France?
2. **Is your browsing actually slow at the moment**, or is it working well enough now that you're on 5G?

My general guidance: if you don't need the VPN, turning it off will likely give you the fastest, most direct connection. If you do need it, try running tasks both with and without it to compare before deciding.

**Suggested order:** turn Data Saver off first, restart your phone, and see how things feel on 5G with the VPN still on. If it's still sluggish, disconnect the VPN and test again — that'll tell you which one, if either, is the culprit.

Let me know what you find, and whether you need the VPN for anything specific. Note that I can't change these settings on your device directly — they'll need to be made in your phone's settings.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me turn off Data Saver first.

turns.thought:
Yes — since you don't need the VPN for anything specific, I'd recommend disconnecting it and re-testing. That's the cleanest way to isolate whether it's costing you speed.

A VPN routes all your traffic through an extra remote server, and while you're roaming in France that can mean a long detour — your data may be traveling back through another country before reaching its destination. That added distance is a very common cause of exactly the "good but not excellent" result you're seeing on an otherwise strong 5G connection.

**Please do this:**

1. Go to **Settings → VPN** (or open your VPN app)
2. **Disconnect** the VPN
3. Wait a few seconds for the lock icon to clear from your status bar
4. **Run the speed test again**

Two other things to keep in mind when you re-test:

- **Signal can fluctuate**, so if the first re-test is close to 27.50, try once or twice more for a fair comparison. Also test from the same spot you've been in, so you're comparing like with like.
- **Being on roaming does impose a ceiling.** You're connecting through a local French partner network rather than our own, so peak speeds abroad can be lower than what you'd get at home — even on 5G. So a "good" result while roaming isn't necessarily a fault; it may just be the realistic upper limit here.

Also, just to set expectations on my side: I can't disconnect the VPN for you or run the test remotely — those need to be done on your device. But once you have the new number, tell me what it reads and I'll help you interpret it.

If speeds jump noticeably, you'll have your answer, and you can leave the VPN off for the rest of your trip. If they stay around 27.50, then the VPN isn't the bottleneck, and we can look at other factors — and I'd also be happy to arrange a callback or transfer you to a specialist who can dig into roaming performance in more depth.

Go ahead and give it a try whenever you're ready.
